## Android

Added in v2.3.0. `bare-dns` sends its DNS protocol queries with c-ares. The c-ares documentation says that on Android 8 and newer, the system's DNS servers can only be read through the application's `ConnectivityManager`, and that the application needs the `ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE` permission. The `ConnectivityManager` has to come from the host application, so the addon asks the host for it.

When the addon first loads in the operating system process, it reads two keys from the [embedder context](/bare/reference/bare/embedder-context): [`bare.android.jvm.v1`](/bare/reference/bare/embedder-context#bareandroidjvmv1) and [`bare.android.context.v1`](/bare/reference/bare/embedder-context#bareandroidcontextv1). It calls `getSystemService("connectivity")` on the application context, then passes the JVM and the `ConnectivityManager` to c-ares. The host must publish both keys before the first addon loads. The thread that loads the addon must be attached to the JVM, because the addon calls `GetEnv()` on it and asserts that the call succeeds. As of bare-kit 2.5.5, [Bare Kit](/bare/reference/bare/bare-kit) publishes `bare.android.jvm.v1` but not `bare.android.context.v1`, so an application that embeds Bare through Bare Kit skips this step unless something else publishes that key.

If either key is not published, or the `ConnectivityManager` cannot be obtained, the addon skips this step without an error. c-ares then has no manager, and its documentation says DNS resolution does not work on Android 8 or newer without one when the application targets API level 26 or higher. `dns.lookup()` uses the operating system's `getaddrinfo()` and does not depend on any of this.
